mercury.name: Mariner 10
mercury.summary: First spacecraft to visit Mercury. Made three flybys in 1974–1975, revealing a heavily cratered, Moon-like surface and a surprisingly strong magnetic field.

mercury.name: MESSENGER
mercury.summary: First spacecraft to orbit Mercury (2011–2015). Confirmed water-ice deposits in permanently shadowed polar craters and mapped the entire surface in detail.

mercury.name: BepiColombo
mercury.summary: Joint ESA–JAXA mission composed of two orbiters. Performing multiple Venus and Mercury gravity assists; expected to enter Mercury orbit in November 2026.

venus.name: Mariner 2
venus.summary: Humanity's first successful interplanetary mission. Flew past Venus in December 1962, confirming surface temperatures exceeding 425 °C and a dense carbon-dioxide atmosphere.

venus.name: Venera 13
venus.summary: Survived on Venus's surface for 127 minutes — a record. Returned the first colour images from the Venusian surface and analysed soil composition in situ.

venus.name: Magellan
venus.summary: Radar-mapped 98 % of Venus's surface at high resolution from 1990 to 1994, revealing thousands of volcanoes, lava plains, and unique 'corona' structures.

venus.name: DAVINCI+
venus.summary: Will drop an instrumented descent sphere through Venus's atmosphere to analyse its composition layer by layer, plus image the enigmatic tessera highlands from orbit.

earth.name: Int'l Space Station
earth.summary: Continuously inhabited since November 2000. Orbiting at ~400 km altitude, it serves as a world-class microgravity laboratory and international cooperation symbol.

earth.name: Hubble Space Telescope
earth.summary: One of the most productive scientific instruments ever built. From low Earth orbit it has produced iconic deep-field images and refined the Hubble constant.

earth.name: James Webb ST
earth.summary: Operating at the L2 Lagrange point, 1.5 million km from Earth. Its 6.5 m gold mirror captures infrared light from the first galaxies and nearby exoplanet atmospheres.

mars.name: Curiosity Rover
mars.summary: Has driven 30+ km inside Gale Crater since landing in 2012. Confirmed ancient lake environments capable of supporting microbial life and detected complex organics.

mars.name: Perseverance Rover
mars.summary: Collecting rock cores in Jezero Crater for a future Earth-return mission. Generated the first oxygen from the Martian atmosphere (MOXIE experiment) in 2021.

mars.name: Ingenuity Helicopter
mars.summary: First powered aircraft on another planet. Exceeded its planned five flights with 72 flights totalling over 2 hours of flight time before a rotor blade was damaged.

mars.name: Hope Probe (Amal)
mars.summary: The Arab world's first interplanetary mission. Orbiting Mars since February 2021, studying its daily and seasonal weather patterns and the escape of hydrogen and oxygen.

jupiter.name: Pioneer 10
jupiter.summary: First spacecraft to cross the asteroid belt and fly past Jupiter (1973). Carried the famous gold-anodized Pioneer plaque bearing a message for any extra-terrestrial finders.

jupiter.name: Voyager 1
jupiter.summary: Flew past Jupiter in 1979, discovering active volcanoes on Io and complex ring structures. Now the most distant human-made object, 24 billion km from the Sun.

jupiter.name: Galileo
jupiter.summary: Orbited Jupiter from 1995 to 2003. Discovered strong evidence for a liquid-water ocean beneath Europa's icy crust and a metallic core inside Io. Deorbited deliberately.

jupiter.name: Juno
jupiter.summary: In a polar orbit that takes it within 4,200 km of Jupiter's cloud tops. Mapping the gravity and magnetic fields to understand what lies beneath the visible atmosphere.

jupiter.name: Europa Clipper
jupiter.summary: Will perform 49 close flybys of Europa from Jupiter orbit, assessing whether its subsurface ocean could support life. Arrives at Jupiter in April 2030.

saturn.name: Pioneer 11
saturn.summary: First spacecraft to visit Saturn (1979). Discovered the F ring and measured temperatures in the upper atmosphere for the first time.

saturn.name: Voyager 2
saturn.summary: Flew past Saturn in 1981. Returned stunning images of the ring structure, revealed braided structures in the F ring, and discovered three previously unknown moons.

saturn.name: Cassini–Huygens
saturn.summary: Orbited Saturn from 2004 to 2017 — 13 remarkable years. The Huygens probe landed on Titan's methane lakes. Discovered active cryo-geysers on Enceladus hinting at a subsurface ocean.

saturn.name: Dragonfly
saturn.summary: A nuclear-powered dual-quadcopter rotorcraft destined for Titan. Will hop between sites to sample the prebiotic chemistry in Titan's nitrogen-rich atmosphere and hydrocarbon seas.

uranus.name: Voyager 2
uranus.summary: The only spacecraft ever to visit Uranus (January 1986). Discovered 10 new moons and 2 new rings, and found that Uranus's magnetic field is oddly tilted 59° from its rotation axis.

neptune.name: Voyager 2
neptune.summary: The only spacecraft ever to visit Neptune (August 1989). Discovered 6 new moons, 4 faint rings, the Great Dark Spot (a storm larger than Earth), and geysers erupting from Triton's surface.
